key_insight: Long tasks do not necessarily require long contexts. Frequent context compaction lets frontier language models maintain short contexts with little to no loss in task accuracy across the tasks studied.
problem_solved: As context grows, generating later tokens becomes more expensive—up to 7× in the frontier open-weight models studied—making long-input and long-horizon workflows costly.
method: Frequently compact accumulated context to keep the model's active context short.
Evaluate accuracy across a broad range of long-input and long-horizon tasks.
Test long-horizon software engineering with at most one action per context to assess performance under aggressive context limits.
impact: Practitioners may be able to reduce inference costs by managing context rather than continually expanding it. The findings suggest that large active contexts are not always necessary, even for extended software engineering workflows.
visual_elements: Token-cost chart highlighting that later tokens can cost up to 7× more than earlier tokens.
Workflow diagram: growing context → compaction → short context → next action.
Accuracy comparison between long-context and frequently compacted workflows, using reported results.
Software engineering timeline showing one action per context across a long task.
paper_authors: Peter Belcak, Saurav Muralidharan, Jindong Jiang, Yonggan Fu, Wonmin Byeon
